english.title: Section 18 - wounding with intent to resist / prevent arrest
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) unlawfully and maliciously wounded **(..SPECIFY PERSON..) with intent to resist or prevent the lawful apprehension or detainer of

(A)_[yourself]_
(B)_[another]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 18of the Offences Against the Person Act 1861.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
unlawfully and maliciously wound a person with intent to resist/prevent lawful apprehension/detainer of self/another

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) See also offence wording: H2294.
(ii) Officers should ensure that they know the C.P.S. guidelines for this offence before preparing any charges. When investigating this offence consideration must be given to the advice offered in the assault charging standards.
(iii) Where this offence is committed against an emergency worker this must be treated as an aggravating factor in sentencing, see section 67 of the Sentencing Act 2020.
(iv) Terrorist connection - this offence is listed in Schedule 1 to the Sentencing Act 2020. Where the court has determined that there is a terrorist connection, the court has to treat this as an aggravating factor in sentencing (section 69 of that Act) and the notification requirements under the Counter-Terrorism Act 2008 apply (section 42 of that Act). In addition, section 23A of the Terrorism Act 2000 provides for forfeiture of money or other property.
(v) See section 72 of the Domestic Abuse Act 2021 regarding the committing of this offence outside the UK by a UK national or a person habitually resident in England and Wales.
